title: Institutions and the Broader Economy Now Drive a Third of Blockchain Revenue
summary:
1kx, a research-driven, fundamentals-focused global investment firm, today released the 1kx Blockchain Revenue Report, the second edition of its annual analysis of blockchain revenues. This year's measure is broader than last year's Onchain Revenue Report, which tracked only onchain user-paid fees. The report now covers all blockchain revenues, including offchain exchange fees, the revenues of public companies, other income such as stablecoin reserve interest, as well as mining and staking rewards.
The report combines onchain data from more than 2,600 protocols, the earnings reports of more than 100 public companies, and additional sources on private entities, through the end of Q3 2026. The full report is available at https://1kx.capital/writing/revenue-report-2026.
Report Findings
Blockchain revenues fell 28% in 2026 but rose again in Q3. Full-year 2026 blockchain revenues are expected to reach about $100 billion, down 28% from roughly $140 billion in 2025 and in line with the decline in digital asset prices - although relative to total digital asset market capitalization, revenues were flat. Onchain user-paid fees were $3.9 billion in Q3 2026 and estimated $14B for all of 2026.
Beneath the drawdown, the mix is changing. Revenues from institutional adoption, meaning revenue earned by institutions as owners (ETF, card network and chain fees) and from institutional clients, were 12% of blockchain revenues in 2026 through Q3, up from 6% in 2021. In dollars, they doubled over three years to $6.1 billion in the first half of 2026, though they fell $0.7 billion year over year as price-sensitive asset management, custody and staking fees declined; their share rose because total revenues fell faster. The report cuts the same total three ways: by who earns it (public companies, 16% in 2026), by what drives it (institutional and broader-economy adoption, 33% in Q3 2026 and 30% for the year) and by sector (blockchain infrastructure, 21% in Q3 2026).
Broader-economy adoption overtakes blockchain infrastructure. Revenues from broader-economy adoption, including tokenized assets, payments and prediction markets, grew 58% year over year in the first half of 2026, led by prediction markets and trading in tokenized real-world assets, and overtook blockchain infrastructure revenues in Q3 2026 for the first time (22% versus 21%). Institutional and broader-economy revenues together reached 33% of blockchain revenues in Q3 2026.
Public companies now earn 16% of blockchain revenues, up from 7% in 2022; the six largest account for about 60% of public-company blockchain revenue. Large banks and traditional finance incumbents that had negligible blockchain revenue three years ago are on track to earn $1B this year. One way this group expands its revenue is via acquisitions - and there have been quite a few lately: BVNK (Mastercard), OpenZeppelin (S&P Global), bitbank (SBI), Zodia Custody (Standard Chartered).
Dividend-paying tokens beat Bitcoin. 1kx's dividend-token index, which tracks protocols that distribute value to token holders, returned 82% through September 30, 2026, versus a 5% decline for Bitcoin; outperforming Bitcoin was rare in recent years. The index figures are hypothetical and based on backtests. A record 283 protocols distributed value to token holders in Q3 2026.
Among protocols, leadership keeps rotating. In YTD Q3 2026, six of the top 20 protocols by onchain fees were not in last year's top 20, and Robinhood Chain became the third-largest ecosystem by fees within a quarter of launch. 
Prediction market fees grew 19x in a year. 1kx estimates prediction market fees at more than $1.5 billion in Q3 2026, up from $86 million in Q3 2025, on roughly $55 billion settled in the quarter, concentrated in Kalshi and Polymarket; most of these fees are not yet traceable onchain, so the figure is an estimate based on Allium data. Robinhood alone reported $173m in events contracts in Q3 2026, up over 6x from a year earlier. A noteworthy shift is how they (and other public companies) are building their own settlement layers and exchanges for these event contracts, such as Robinhood Chain. 
Payment card spend tripled. Spend on digital asset payment cards tripled year over year to $3.4 billion in Q3 2026, almost all of it on Visa's network.
Tokenized stocks ascendant as markets move 24/7. Volume in tokenized stocks on Robinhood Chain passed $13 billion in Q3 2026, over 70% of it while US exchanges were closed, before Nasdaq moves to 23-hour trading in December. RWA perp volume also increased 122x YoY in Q3 2026.
"The end of the bull market in 2025 also marked a peak in blockchain revenues, but the more important story is underneath the drawdown," said Robert Koschig, Head of Economics at 1kx. "We’ve seen a shift towards fundamentals, with revenues tied to institutional and broader-economy adoption reaching about a third of blockchain revenues in the third quarter. That growth comes with rising activity and ownership from traditional finance across the full stack, from infrastructure to applications. 
“Tokenized stocks trading around the clock, prediction markets inside brokerage apps, and payment volume on card networks signal the convergence of traditional finance and digital assets in practice. For us as investors, the data confirms where we focus: on the fundamentals. We look for areas where legacy structures cannot yet deliver and where an intermediary's take is compressible, and onchain data is how we track that in real time.”
1kx publishes the Blockchain Revenue Report annually and updates its revenue dashboard monthly at https://1kx.capital/onchain-revenue-dashboard.

Despite overall blockchain revenues falling 28% in 2026, sectors like prediction markets, tokenized assets, and payment card spending experienced massive growth. Traditional finance companies and public firms are increasing their presence, with large banks on track to earn substantial revenues as digital assets and traditional finance continue to converge.

title: Asia’s CFOs Still Build Their Cash Position by Hand, Finmo Advisory Board Finds
summary:
Finance leaders across Singapore and Southeast Asia don’t observe their cash position. They assemble it, by hand, from bank and investment portals, emailed statements and spreadsheets, on a schedule set by the combination of their cash flow profile and capacity to assemble. 
That is the central finding of What CFOs Really Need from Treasury Technology, a white paper published today by Finmo as convener of its CFO & Treasurer Advisory Board. The paper draws on two Board sessions in Singapore in May and July 2026 and two interviews with each Board member between June and September. Contributors include Junxiong Ho, Group CFO, Funding Societies; Iris Ho, CFO, Insignia Ventures; Pei Pei Tam, CFO, Edenred; Shi Mei Chin, Found & CEO, CFOi; and Dominic Ong, CFO & Head of Strategic Partnerships, Endowus. 
The board is responsible for finance and often other functions for their firms. Their businesses represent multiple industries, geographies, regulated and non-regulated businesses, and range from growth-stage companies to large multinationals. Different businesses, balance sheets and regulators, but their treasury and cash operations and the challenges they face were very consistent. 
Six findings 
● The position is assembled, not observed. In some teams, 80 to 90 percent of the work runs on Excel, fed by portals, emails, the ERP and the treasury system. The position is only as current as the last rebuild, and may not survive the holiday of the person who builds it. 
● Multi-entity, not multi-currency, is the unsolved problem. Accounting platforms are single-entity by design and lag one to two weeks until transactions are coded. The multi-entity view the board requires takes the longest to produce and as a result contains less up-to-date information when it arrives. 
● Forecasting tools answer the wrong question. For several members, inflows can’t be usefully predicted. What they need to know is what must go out – payroll, tax, large invoices, settlement runs – and whether every entity can cover it. 
● The decision that matters sits outside every tool. Target balances, built from bank minimums, operating needs, buffers and regulatory floors, live in spreadsheets and rarely change. Buffers stay conservative and cash sits idle. 
● FX risk arrives as an explanation, not a warning. Firms without in-house FX expertise often find their exposure after supplier payments settle, when it is already a cost. 
● AI drafts, people approve. Members already use AI for month-end close, collection emails and payment instructions across dozens of entities, with a person reviewing every entry. Where systems are patchily connected, AI becomes one more report built on incomplete data.
“These are not unsophisticated teams with bad tools. Several have excellent tools,” said Thomas Kang, Co-Founder and Chief Strategy Officer, Finmo, who convenes the board. “One runs an enterprise treasury management system and still builds the working position in a spreadsheet next to it. The problem is not the tools. It is the space between them.” 
Built with the board, and what comes next 
The paper also shows the board’s input already at work in Finmo’s product. Six capabilities shipped between July and September 2026 in direct response to board requests, including a single cash view across accounts, currencies and entities, and minimum balance alerts by account, bank, or entity. It then sets out, openly, the next priorities the board has put on the table: bulk and recurring payment initiation with automatic reconciliation, back-testing forecasts against actuals by horizon, intercompany and in-house bank mechanics, and FX hedge capacity modelling. 
“We had been treating visibility as the product and the constraint as configuration. The board reversed that,” said Michael Kolman, Vice President, Product Management, Finmo. “The target balance, the regulatory floor, the policy cap, the credit line – that’s what turns a balance into a decision. It belongs in the system, not in the spreadsheet beside it.” The paper closes with a four-stage benchmark, from Assembled to Directed, and eleven questions finance leaders can put to any treasury technology vendor, or to the tools they already use. The first one to ask: what does it cost to add my next bank, and who pays to keep that connection running?

title: Santander Announces a 5% Increase in the Exchange Ratio for Its Intended Exchange Offer for the Outstanding Shares of Santander Brasil
summary:
Banco Santander has decided to enhance the terms announced on 30 July 2026 for the voluntary offer it intends to launch to acquire all of Santander Brasil’s issued and outstanding common shares, preferred shares, units and American Depositary Shares (ADSs) that it does not already own, representing approximately 10% of Santander Brasil’s share capital (through concurrent exchange offers in Brazil and the US), following recent market developments and feedback from stakeholders.
Banco Santander has increased the previously announced exchange ratio by 5% to make the offer more attractive for holders of Santander Brasil securities. Holders who tender their securities will now receive (i) for each unit or ADS of Santander Brasil, 0.4260 newly issued Banco Santander shares (instead of the 0.4056 announced on 30 July) and (ii) for each common share or preferred share[1] of Santander Brasil, 0.2130 newly issued Banco Santander shares (instead of the 0.2028 announced on 30 July)[2].
After adjusting for the dividends already paid by Banco Santander and Santander Brasil since 30 July 2026, the exchange ratios as at today's date would be 0.4246 Banco Santander shares per unit or ADS, 0.2124 per common share and 0.2122 per preferred share of Santander Brasil, already reflecting the improvement announced today. In all cases, the Banco Santander shares will continue to be delivered in the form of Brazilian Depositary Receipts (BDRs) or ADSs, as applicable, which will be tradable on the São Paulo stock exchange and the New York Stock Exchange, respectively.
Assuming full acceptance of the offer, Banco Santander would issue approximately 166 million new shares, equivalent to approximately 1.1% of its current share capital and the maximum consideration would be approximately €1.9 billion, based on yesterday’s closing market price.
Banco Santander will seek shareholders’ approval for the corresponding capital increases to settle the offer at an extraordinary general shareholders’ meeting that is expected to be held on 15 December 2026.
As previously indicated, the transaction is fully aligned with Santander's strategy of delivering long-term shareholder value creation and meets the group's disciplined capital allocation framework. It compares favourably with alternative deployment options, while remaining capital neutral. Considering the revised terms of the offer, the transaction is expected to increase earnings per share by approximately 0.3% from 2029 and tangible book value per share by approximately 0.6%, as well as to generate an attractive return on invested capital, based on current market expectations. It is also expected to strengthen the group's long-term earnings growth and to enhance its capacity for organic capital generation in the years ahead.
For Santander Brasil's minority shareholders, the offer provides an attractive opportunity to realize the value of their investment at a premium to the market price, now on improved terms compared with those announced on 30 July. At the same time, it enables them to become shareholders in one of the world's leading diversified financial groups, with a broader earnings base, resilient profitability and a proven track record of sustainable value creation.
Commencement of the offer and the offer itself will be subject to customary conditions for transactions of this nature, including the obtaining of the relevant regulatory approvals, the approval by Banco Santander’s extraordinary general shareholders’ meeting of the corresponding capital increases and the absence of any material adverse change.
[1] Each Santander Brasil unit is composed of one ordinary share and one preferred share.
[2] Subject to certain adjustments for certain events that may occur between 30 July 2026 and the expiration of the offer, including potential dividends, interest on equity and/or share bonuses paid by Banco Santander and/or Santander Brasil and/or stock splits and/or reverse stock splits by either of them. Share buybacks conducted during such period shall not cause adjustment of the exchange ratio.

content: Banco Santander has announced a 5 percent increase in the exchange ratio for its voluntary offer to acquire the remaining minority shares of Santander Brasil. title: Spotlight on Speed: Half of Payments on Swift Reach Banks Within 40 Seconds, but Domestic Delays Impact User Experience
summary:
Swift today published new data which reveals that half of transactions across its network reach recipient institutions within 40 seconds, as the financial industry makes strong progress towards the G20’s goal for the speed of cross-border payments.
 
The figures reflect a continued drive by Swift and the industry to make international payments fast, predictable and as seamless as the best domestic ones. Since June, banks globally have been using Swift’s retail payments framework to deliver a best-in-class experience along some of the world’s busiest payments routes, including to five of the biggest remittance-receiving markets. Under the framework, transactions have been completed end-to-end in minutes and even seconds—including from Turkey to Spain in 15 seconds, Australia to India in 37 seconds, and from Brazil to the US in just a minute.
 
However, Swift’s research has shown that while inter-bank processing times are fast, end customers don’t always benefit because of frictions that occur between a payment arriving at the receiving institution and being credited to the beneficiary’s account. This final stage of a transaction, known as the ‘last mile’, accounts for 80% of the average transaction’s total journey time.
 
Swift’s latest Spotlight on Speed report focuses on the drivers of delays and where improvements can be made, revealing wide variation in last mile processing times. The report analysed 40 receiving markets and found that in a third, median processing time between the receiving institution and the beneficiary account is around an hour. But in others, there is a mixed picture with fast payments existing alongside significantly slower transactions.
 
The findings highlight where co-ordinated action by the industry and regulators can help translate faster cross-border processing into a more consistent experience for customers. Swift’s report recommends that the industry prioritises ‘one-leg-out’ arrangements, which enable in-country instant payment systems to process the domestic leg of international payments. Swift’s global network already enables fast cross-border payments to some markets under one-leg-out agreements, with its end-to-end tracking capabilities extended across the domestic leg.
 

Thierry Chilosi, Chief Business Officer at Swift, said: “Cross-border processing speeds are consistently fast, but if we’re to deliver the experience that customers expect then the challenge now is to tackle the inconsistency that we see in the last mile in markets around the world. As we’ve shown over the last few months, connecting Swift’s trusted infrastructure with domestic instant payment systems is driving improvements in speed, predictability and transparency—so if we want to scale the improvements we’ve been making then these one-leg-out arrangements should absolutely be a priority.”
 
As well as working to bring the cross-border experience in line with what consumers have come to expect domestically, Swift is also enabling the benefits of digital finance to be experienced globally by its network of 12,500 institutions across 200+ markets. By the end of the year, 19 early-adopter financial institutions will have made use of Swift’s blockchain ledger for tokenised deposit transactions, using five major currencies.

title: Chargebacks911 Warns Merchants of Three-Way Returns Trap
summary:
Black Friday is coming and for most retailers, the returns conversation is already the wrong one, according to Chargebacks911, a global leader in dispute resolution and chargeback management.
The industry is focused on how to tighten policies, add friction and cut losses and that is understandable. According to Appriss Retail's 2026 Total Retail Loss Benchmark Report, US retailers processed $706 billion in returns last year, of which $100 billion, or 14.2%, represented preventable fraud and abuse. That splits into $14 billion in outright fraud and $86 billion in policy abuse: wardrobing, bracketing and the full spectrum of behaviors that exploit generous return windows without technically breaking any laws.
The response from merchants has been logical: tighten up. Add return fees, narrow the window and require proof of purchase but the problem is that the results are anything but straightforward. The NRF and Happy Returns 2025 Retail Returns Landscape Report found that nearly two-thirds of consumers admit to at least one costly returns behavior anyway. And separate research reported by eMarketer found that 44% of merchants who introduced return fees saw fraud go up, compared with only 42% who saw it fall.
The commercial consequences extend beyond fraud losses - according to Appriss Retail's 2026 Total Retail Loss Benchmark Report, eight in ten shoppers say a positive returns experience makes them more likely to purchase from a retailer again. Tightening returns policies may help address abuse, but retailers also need to consider how those changes affect legitimate customers and future sales.
"Here is the trap retailers keep falling into," said Monica Eaton, Founder and CEO of Chargebacks911. "They make returns easier and abuse goes up. They make returns harder and customers walk away. And some of that dissatisfaction can resurface as a chargeback instead. That is not necessarily a better outcome as it can be a more expensive problem dressed up as a solution."
The chargeback consequence matters because it is not always immediately visible. Chargebacks911's 2026 Chargeback Field Report, found that 27.1% of merchant returns already involve some form of refund abuse. And 61.8% of merchants report that chargebacks have increased over the past three years, with friendly fraud growing faster than overall chargeback volumes.
"We talk to merchants every day who are absorbing losses from both sides," said Eaton. "Returns abuse on one side, chargebacks on the other. Treating them as completely separate problems makes it much harder to see the patterns connecting them. If you only look at one side of the customer journey, you are only seeing half the problem."
The merchants who handle this period most effectively are not those with the strictest return policies but those that can see the connection between what happens at the point of return and what happens weeks later in the dispute system, which customers are appearing in both, which patterns are repeating and where an earlier conversation with a customer might have prevented a chargeback entirely.
"Peak season is not the time to discover that your returns data and your dispute data live in different systems and nobody is looking at both," said Eaton. "The question retailers should be asking right now is not how do I stop returns but has to be how do I tell the difference between a genuine customer and a pattern of behavior that is costing me money. That distinction is where the problem actually gets solved."

title: Creditstar Group Launches First Credit Card Under Monefit Brand
summary:
Creditstar Group, a European consumer finance and investment fintech, has launched its first credit card under the Monefit brand in Estonia, extending the group’s consumer lending offering into card-based spending. The public launch follows a controlled rollout to waiting-list customers that began in August.
The card adds a product for everyday spending to the group’s existing instalment loans and revolving credit. Creditstar Group has provided consumer credit since 2006 and today operates lending businesses in the UK and seven EU markets, with over 1.9 million registered customers. 
The Monefit Card was largely built on the group’s existing modular technology platform, connecting the card programme to the underwriting, risk, compliance and servicing infrastructure already used across its lending businesses. The group developed card-specific capabilities including card and transaction management, scheme and processor integrations, in-app card controls and digital-wallet integration.
“Our lending products have traditionally been used when someone has a specific financing need; a card gives Monefit a place in everyday spending and creates a much more frequent relationship with customers,” said Aaro Sosaar, founder and CEO of Creditstar Group.
“The card also demonstrates how we can use our existing technology infrastructure to develop new products without having to rebuild core systems from scratch. Estonia is our first deployment, but we now have a foundation that can be adapted for other markets as we assess further expansion,” Sosaar added.
The credit card carries a fixed annual interest rate of 20% for every approved customer, with no annual, monthly or application fee. Approved customers receive a virtual Mastercard immediately, can order a physical card, and can manage their account through the Monefit app. Google Pay is supported, with Apple Pay support to follow.
The group is also developing Flex, a buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) feature that will allow cardholders to convert eligible purchases into fixed-term instalment plans. Flex is expected to be introduced in the coming months, giving customers an additional option to spread the cost of purchases. 
The Monefit app includes a Payment Wheel showing how different repayment amounts affect customers’ balance and interest before payment, including the amounts needed to meet the minimum payment, avoid interest or clear the balance.
“We designed Monefit Card around making the cost of credit easier to understand at the point customers decide how to repay. The aim is to give them clearer choices and more control over how they use and repay their balance. Flex will add another option by allowing eligible purchases to be converted into fixed instalments,” said Kashyap Shah, Chief Product Officer at Creditstar Group.  
The Monefit Card is a Creditstar Group product, with Monefit Estonia OÜ providing the consumer credit, assessing applications and managing the programme. Moorwand Ltd, a principal member of Mastercard International, provides the programme’s Mastercard scheme partnership, while Thredd provides the issuer processing infrastructure.
The product expansion follows a record year for Creditstar Group. According to its latest audited annual accounts, published in June 2026, the group increased interest income by 49.8% to €110.9 million and net profit by 86% to €13.5 million. Its net loan portfolio after provisions stood at  €482 million at year-end.

title: BMLL and Vola Dynamics Partner to Bring Market-Maker-Quality Options Analytics to Unified Historical Data in a Fully Managed Research Environment
summary:
BMLL, the global market data and analytics platform provider, today announced a strategic partnership with Vola Dynamics, the options analytics provider that market makers, banks, and hedge funds use to price options, model volatility and manage risk. 
The collaboration integrates Vola’s options analytics library directly with BMLL’s historical market data within the BMLL Data Lab, combining BMLL’s deep, clean, historical options and underlying market data with Vola’s volatility and pricing library inside a single managed environment.  Quantitative hedge funds are able to run scenarios, market makers can reconstruct historical vol surfaces and validate hedging strategies, and asset managers can add  volatility fitting, pricing and scenario analysis to their historical market research without the need to build separate data or analytics workflows. 
Options and Volatility Research Infrastructure Challenges
Building and maintaining an in-house pipeline to clean options and underlying data, snapshot it, fit volatility surfaces, and compute risk is slow, expensive, and specialist work. Historically, quantitative research teams have faced significant technical barriers in assembling clean historical options data and market-maker-quality fitting, pricing, and risk workflows within the same research environment. This technical friction often forces quants to spend substantial development time managing data infrastructure and maintaining software libraries rather than focusing on core research.
Responding to Market Demand for Integrated Options Analytics
As options and volatility become a core research focus driven by increased listed options activity and the growth of volatility as an asset class, research teams increasingly want to reduce the lead time needed for systematic options research.
BMLL and Vola Dynamics significantly reduce this technical barrier by enabling research teams to apply Vola’s volatility surface fitting, theoretical pricing, Greeks and scenario analysis directly to BMLL options and underlying data within the BMLL Data Lab. Rather than managing two separate systems or operating complex data-cleaning pipelines, researchers can quickly move from historical market data to fitted volatility surfaces, theoretical prices, and risk metrics in minutes.
To access the capability, clients run Vola's library directly inside the BMLL Data Lab using their own Vola license. Under this structure, researchers can use BMLL’s underlying historical dataset, and the Vola library to transform raw data into arbitrage free volatility surfaces, clean valuations, and realistic scenarios. 
Paul Humphrey, CEO of BMLL, said: "As listed options activity grows and volatility becomes an increasingly vital asset class, quantitative teams need to move fast without getting bogged down by infrastructure. By integrating Vola’s options analytics directly within the BMLL Data Lab, we are removing the heavy plumbing work of cleaning data and maintaining the options analytics stack. title: Imprint Raises $130 Million to Help Brands Build Customer Loyalty as AI Reshapes Commerce
summary:
Imprint, the payments, loyalty, and customer intelligence platform brands use to make every transaction more valuable, has raised $130 million in new financing, valuing the company at approximately $1.9 billion. The round was led by existing investor Khosla Ventures, with participation from existing investors Hedosophia, Ribbit Capital, Spice, Thrive Capital, and new investor Positive Sum. The funding will support the company’s expansion into new payment options and AI capabilities that help brands recognize and reward customers wherever and however they choose to pay.
 
Imprint now serves more than two million members and partners with brands representing more than $500 billion in annual U.S. consumer spending. Since the beginning of the year, Imprint has launched programs with Albertsons Companies, Fanatics, Kroger, and Shell, with the Fanatics program debuting this week. Across Imprint’s partner portfolio, total cardholder spending more than doubled between 2025 and 2026. The share of spending on Imprint cards at partner checkouts tripled over the past year. Imprint also recently added $1.5 billion in incremental warehouse capacity and priced its second AAA-rated asset-backed securitization, with investor demand nearly five times the offering size.
 
As AI changes how people discover, compare, and buy, brands face new challenges in maintaining direct customer relationships. Agentic commerce is projected to mediate up to $1 trillion in U.S. retail revenue by 2030. Imprint brings payments, loyalty, and customer intelligence together so brands can learn from everyday spending and deliver recognition and rewards that give customers reasons to return.
 

“From AI chats to personal agents, every digital touchpoint is quickly becoming personalized. In this future, the brands that invest in understanding who their customers really are, and building relationships with each individually, will win,” said Daragh Murphy, founder and CEO of Imprint. “Imprint helps brands create financial products to earn a place in their customers’ everyday lives, and make them feel like a regular, uniquely recognizing and rewarding them for their loyalty. The latest round supports our growth as we build more ways for brands to meet customers where they are, regardless of how they want to shop or pay.”
 
To help brands adapt as more consumers use AI assistants to manage their finances and make purchases, Imprint has released a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that allows AI agents to securely access members’ rewards, virtual cards, and transaction history, along with tools for members to review and authorize agent-initiated purchases. Internally, Imprint’s AI platform has tripled engineering velocity, the rate at which the company turns ideas into production software, in the past 18 months.
 

“AI will make every option easier to compare, which makes earning a customer’s preference more valuable than ever,” said Patrick O’Shaughnessy, CEO and Partner at Positive Sum. “Imprint gives brands a way to earn that preference every day through payments and rewards. Daragh and the team built the full-stack technology themselves, have proven their ability to win marquee partners, and are growing quickly. That combination gives us conviction that they can capture a much bigger opportunity from here.”
 
Founded in 2020, Imprint built the technology behind co-branded credit cards from the ground up. The company owns its stack across origination, risk, servicing, and rewards, giving brands control over their financial products and the flexibility to tailor rewards, offers, and experiences to their customers.
 
Following the recent unveiling of the new Fanatics American Express® Card, Glenn H. Schiffman, EVP, Chief Financial Officer and Director of Fanatics, said, “With Imprint, we can offer a card that creates a new way to deepen our relationships with fans and provide a value proposition to sports fans that doesn’t exist in the market — and that is rewarding their passion — in a product that feels distinctly Fanatics. Imprint’s technology and approach made it possible to design a program around our fans and our business in a way no other provider could.”
 

“Imprint has been a great partner to Fetch. They have a dedicated team that cares about making our program successful, consistently brings us new products and capabilities, and is always willing to dig into new ideas with us. With Imprint, we’re seeing stronger engagement from cardholders, which translates into greater loyalty and lifetime value. I’m proud of what we’ve built together and excited to keep building,” said Rachel Ehrlich, General Manager at Fetch.
 
The funding will also help Imprint extend its products to more of its partners’ customers. The 10 largest U.S. co-branded credit card programs alone account for more than $1.1 trillion in payment value, yet traditional credit products remain difficult to access for some loyal customers. An estimated 32 million Americans have little or no credit history. Backed by a refundable deposit, Imprint Access, launching today, gives eligible customers who are new to credit or rebuilding their credit access to the same ongoing rewards as their favorite brands’ unsecured cards. With responsible use, customers can build credit and work toward upgrading to an unsecured credit card.

title: Salad Secures £1.5 Million City Bridge Foundation Investment to Expand Affordable Credit Across London
summary:
Salad, the UK’s largest consumer lending Community Development Finance Institution (CDFI), has secured a £1.5 million social impact investment from City Bridge Foundation, enabled by a £1.2 million funding guarantee from Fair4All Finance. The partnership will unlock up to £20 million in affordable and responsible lending capacity, helping more Londoners access fair credit when they are unable to do so through mainstream providers.
The investment will support Salad's mission to widen access to affordable credit for people who are underserved by traditional lenders despite often having stable incomes and manageable borrowing needs. It follows a recent close of over £1.6 million on Ethex, the impact investing platform, twice Salad’s initial target. This means retail investors have now committed just under £6 million to support Salad, the largest cumulative raise of any CDFI on the platform.
Rather than relying solely on historic credit scores, Salad uses Open Banking technology to assess an individual's current financial circumstances and affordability. Founded in 2018, it has lent more than £300 million to over 200,000 customers and earlier this year received a King's Award for Enterprise, recognising its innovation in fair and affordable lending. As demand for accessible and responsible credit continues to grow, the new funding will support Salad’s continued growth and expand its reach across London's communities.
Research from Fair4All Finance shows that 46% of Londoners currently have low financial resilience, and affordable credit remains out of reach for many households. The partnership demonstrates how mission-led investors, funders and lenders can work together to tackle financial exclusion at scale, at a time when household finances are increasingly stretched.
The investment comes through Fair4All Finance's Guarantees Pilot for Affordable Credit, which uses funding guarantees as one instrument to encourage new sources of investment into the community finance sector. By reducing risk for investors, the model is designed to unlock capital that might not otherwise be available to support affordable lending.
Craig Pennington, CEO of Salad, said:
"This investment is a significant milestone for Salad and an important vote of confidence in our mission to make fair and affordable credit accessible to more people who are overlooked by mainstream lenders. We see every day the challenges faced by people who need access to credit but are excluded by traditional approaches to lending. The backing of City Bridge Foundation, alongside the support of our long-term partner Fair4All Finance, will enable us to reach more Londoners and continue building a financial system that works for people who have too often been left behind."
Paul Martinelli, Chair of the City Bridge Foundation Board said: 
“Most Londoners can borrow at a fair price when they need to. But many people on low incomes can’t and can end up paying far more for the same loan. Salad offers affordable credit to people who are too often turned away by banks. 
"This is one of City Bridge Foundation’s first social investments in financial inclusion and lets our resources work harder for London. By helping Londoners borrow fairly, we hope to give them greater financial security and more room to plan ahead." 
David Coombs, Director of Investment at Fair4All Finance said:
“We’re delighted to provide this funding guarantee to City Bridge Foundation and look forward to the positive impact this new lending capacity will deliver for Salad customers across London. By de-risking investments like this one, our Guarantees Pilot for Affordable Credit helps bring new funders in to back responsible lenders and contributes to closing the affordable credit gap by expanding fair and affordable options for households.”

Mr. Lin Jincan, President, GCC Region, Huawei

title: Finastra and Coefficient Markets Bridge Trading and Operations to Accelerate Loan Trade Booking
summary:
Finastra and Coefficient Markets today announced a partnership to modernize corporate loan trading workflows. The collaboration links Coefficient’s dealer workflow system, EPIC, with Finastra’s Loan IQ to automate loan trade capture and booking, improving connectivity between trade and downstream operations.
 
Why Finastra and Coefficient Markets are partnering - less manual work and more time for trading
 
As part of the partnership, EPIC will integrate directly with Finastra’s Loan IQ Nexus APIs, allowing trades captured in EPIC to flow automatically into Loan IQ for booking. Supporting single-trade, bulk and portfolio trade bookings, EPIC helps create a more efficient process from trade capture through back-office processing.
 
For trading desks and their counterparties, this means faster trade processing, improved accuracy and less manual data entry, giving teams more time to focus on trading and investment decisions rather than operational administration. The integration also helps improve data consistency across the loan lifecycle and enables dealers to support higher trading volumes and greater market liquidity more efficiently.
 
Executive perspective: Supporting trading growth with less manual work
 

“Secondary loan trading activity has grown more than 40% since 2023, and trade counts have grown even faster, yet many dealer workflows still rely on manual processes, spreadsheets and disconnected systems,” said Brian Callahan, CEO of Coefficient Markets. “As trading activity has grown, the need to connect the systems used to manage the front-office workflow with the systems used to book those trades has become increasingly important. With this partnership, we’re bringing those processes together. EPIC and Loan IQ help eliminate unnecessary re-keying, improve data quality and give dealers a more efficient way to manage growing trading volumes and market complexity.”
 

Robert Downs, Loan IQ Product Head at Finastra, added, “Finastra continues to expand its ecosystem of technology partners to help financial institutions modernize lending operations. By combining Coefficient Markets’ dealer workflow capabilities with the power of Loan IQ, we’re helping customers create a more connected trading process from capture through booking. The result is reduced manual effort, stronger data integrity and greater operational efficiency.”
 
This collaboration also builds on the partnerships that Finastra and Coefficient Markets have established with S&P Global Market Intelligence across the corporate and syndicated lending ecosystem. Together, these integrations help connect workflows across the trade lifecycle, from trade inception through settlement. Together, Finastra, Coefficient Markets, and S&P are creating a more connected secondary loan trading ecosystem, linking dealer workflows, servicing, and post-trade processes.

title: NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition
summary:
NVIDIA Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately.
Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates.
Kress has served as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA since joining the company in September 2013. During her tenure, she has led the company’s finance organization and has played a key role in NVIDIA’s growth and evolution. Prior to joining NVIDIA, Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft.
The Board of Directors appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever Chair of the Board.  Mr. Jones has been an entrepreneur, technology executive, and active venture investor for over 30 years, including serving as Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of Synopsys.
“Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” said Harvey Jones, Chair of the NVIDIA Board of Directors. “She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing NVIDIA’s strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.”  
“NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” said Colette Kress, Interim CEO and CFO, NVIDIA. “We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.” 
Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.
NVIDIA will report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results on Tuesday, November 17, at approximately 1:20 p.m. PT, as previously scheduled, followed by its earnings call at 2 p.m. PT.
